nominees_pass2.stem_excerpt: Start with the graph of y=x². Your team may apply any combination of: vertical stretch/compress by a≠0, reflect in the x-axis, translate horizontally by h, translate vertically by k. Produce three different graphs that all pass through the point (2,5). For each, give an equation in the form y=a(x-h)²+k and explain how you know (2,5) works. Then: which parameters are forced by (2,5), and which stay free?

nominees_pass2.stem_excerpt: A school fountain shoots water along a path that can be modelled by y = -0.2(x-3)² + 4.5, where x is horizontal distance in metres from a wall and y is height in metres above the ground. The nozzle is attached at the wall (x=0 is not necessarily the nozzle — teams must interpret). Using a graph or table: (1) What heights are possible for the water? (2) For which horizontal distances does the model even make sense in this courtyard if the far wall is at x=8 m and water cannot go underground? Defend your domain and range with the graph — not by formula first.
nominees_pass2.revisit_upgrade: Invent bounds from graph/context → domain/range language (A2.3/A2.4). Leave unresolved: solving by formula; full modelling cycle (M3/M4).
nominees_pass2.why_m1: Native ask is domain/range + context restrictions on a quadratic graph.
nominees_pass2.why_not_elsewhere: If treated as max-height formula / zeros, park M3/M4 — keep graph-first rule.
